solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Writer almost prepared to accept plagiarism

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece holds the other inside it
almost means the word for prepared is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: prepared means set, as in all set
to crib is to copy someone else's work, so a crib is plagiarism

explanation.surface: An author nearly ready to own up to copying someone else's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SET to SE, and 'to accept' has SE take in CRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a copyist or clerk, and loosely any person who writes for a living.

clue.text: Start of spring with a chill in Mediterranean location

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here from spring

parts.note: icily means coldly, with a chill

explanation.surface: Early spring brings cold weather to a southern European spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The island at the toe of Italy lies in the Mediterranean Sea.

clue.text: Regarding length over Scottish course? Excellent for run

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning
Ayr is a Scottish racecourse
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A query about the distance of a Scottish track, praised as great for running.
explanation.walkthrough: AYR is a horse-racing course on Scotland's west coast; 'over' only places RE and L above it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay race is a team running event in which runners hand on a baton.

clue.text: Essential one Conservative supports party, mostly

indicators.note: in a down clue, supports means sitting underneath, so the other pieces come after the party word
mostly means the word for party loses its last letter

parts.note: a bash is a party
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A key Tory figure backs the party, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts BASH to BAS; 'supports' just places I and C below it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means fundamental, forming the base, so it is a synonym of essential.

clue.text: A very regular writer, skipping intro, may be a cagey type

indicators.note: skipping the intro means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a diarist writes in a journal regularly, day after day

explanation.surface: A habitual journal keeper who leaves out the introduction might be a secretive person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cagey' usually means guarded or secretive; here it is taken literally as someone who deals in cages, and 'skipping intro' takes the D off DIARIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper of birds houses them in an aviary, a large cage, so the person is literally a cage type.

clue.text: Suggestive behaviour, maybe, with French kept in proportion

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the abbreviation goes within the phrase

parts.note: vulgar means crude or suggestive
action means conduct or behaviour

explanation.surface: Racy conduct, perhaps, with the French language kept within limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in proportion' looks like one phrase meaning balanced, but 'kept in' is the containment signal and 'proportion' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulgar fraction such as three quarters expresses a ratio of numerator to denominator.

clue.text: Something you shouldn't attempt when prepared to save face

indicators.note: to save means to keep hold of, so the word for when holds the face inside

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
mug is slang for face
game means willing or prepared, as in 'game for anything'

explanation.surface: Something not worth trying when you are ready to avoid embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to save face' reads as an idiom about keeping dignity, but 'to save' is the containment signal and 'face' is just the word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointless or foolish activity is one only a fool, a mug, would take on.

clue.text: Principle that is engaging Democrat most of all

indicators.note: engaging means holding within, so the abbreviation takes the letter inside

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: most of means the word all loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A tenet that draws in a Democratic politician above all.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a standard or value one lives by, so it is a guiding principle.

clue.text: Band to adorn recording system

parts.note: a tape is a narrow band of material
to deck is to adorn, as in deck the halls

explanation.surface: A musical group decorates its studio sound equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape deck plays and records sound on magnetic tape cassettes or reels.

clue.text: What'll be anodyne news, I'd fancy, around end of year?

definitions.text: What'll be anodyne news, I'd fancy, around end of year?

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to reimagine, signalling a rearrangement of the letters
around, paired with fancy, means the news letters are moved about into a new order
the end of a word is its last letter, here from year

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a sensation will be dull news by December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' and 'around' together rearrange the letters, and 'end of' picks the last of year to close the answer. Read whole, the clue describes the answer: a sensation that soon goes stale.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-lived sensation soon forgotten becomes old, bland news in no time.

clue.text: Heavenly room accommodating one in fancy seat

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the word for room holds the rest inside

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a monk's or prison cell

indicators.note: in places the letter for one within the rearranged seat
fancy as a verb means to elaborate or reimagine, signalling a rearrangement of seat

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A divine chamber with a single person sitting on an ornate chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges seat, 'in' puts the numeral among those letters to make ESTIA, and 'accommodating' houses that in the room word before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial describes things of the sky or of heaven, a direct synonym of heavenly.

clue.text: Exhaust American power restraining group of countries

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so the outer pieces contain the group

parts.note: US is short for American, as in the US
P is the physics symbol for power
the EU, the European Union, is a group of countries

explanation.surface: American might hemming in a bloc of nations wears it out.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust a supply is to consume all of it, leaving none.

clue.text: Impress after releasing singular song

indicators.note: after releasing means once one letter has been let go from the word

parts.note: to slay someone is slang for impressing them hugely, as in 'you slay me'
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A performer wows the audience after letting go of a solo number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impress' looks like a verb about stamping or awing; it gives SLAY, and 'after releasing' drops the S for singular.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay is an old word for a ballad or narrative poem meant to be sung.

clue.text: Foreign areas sadly kept back in recording meal option

indicators.note: kept, completed by in, means held inside, so the disc abbreviation surrounds the rest
in completes the containment signal begun by kept, placing the pieces within

parts.note: a CD, a compact disc, is a recording

indicators.note: foreign means strange or alien, so the letters of areas are made strange by rearranging
back means the word for sadly is read from right to left

parts.note: alas is an exclamation said sadly

explanation.surface: Overseas regions, regrettably, are stored in an archived recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' rearranges areas, 'back' turns round the exclamation, and 'kept ... in' puts both within the disc; 'meal option' is the definition, not part of the recording.
explanation.definitionFit: This salad of romaine, croutons and parmesan is a standard choice on a restaurant menu.

clue.text: "Reduced Beauty Treatment" covering small shop sign

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the trimmed treatment surrounds the letter for small
reduced means cut down, so the treatment loses its last letter

parts.note: a facial is a beauty treatment for the face
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A bargain spa offer is advertised on a little shopfront board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' cuts FACIAL to FACIA, which 'covering' wraps round S. A fascia is the nameboard above a British shopfront.
explanation.definitionFit: The fascia is the board over a shop's front bearing its name, so it is a sign.

clue.text: Weaponry: clubs, historic — a bargain, we hear

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
old means historic, of the past

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like another, here a bargain

parts.note: a steal is a bargain

explanation.surface: An arms list: clubs, an antique piece and a cheap buy, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold steel means bladed weapons such as swords and bayonets, as opposed to firearms.

clue.text: Wild financier finally not in favour of investing in soccer team

indicators.note: investing in means putting into, so the pieces go inside the club abbreviation

parts.note: FC stands for Football Club, a soccer team

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of financier

parts.note: anti means opposed to, not in favour of

explanation.surface: A reckless money man, against the idea at last, puts cash into a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing in' suggests finance to match the financier, but here it means putting the pieces inside the club; 'finally' takes the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic means frenzied or out of control with worry, much as wild does.

clue.text: Hitch? Then fix web image

parts.note: to thumb a lift is to hitch a ride
to nail is to fix in place

explanation.surface: A glitch? Then repair the picture on the website.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hitch' looks like a snag, but it means hitchhike.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail is a small preview picture on a web page.

clue.text: Small missile making a loud noise

parts.note: Trident is a nuclear missile

explanation.surface: A little rocket goes off with a bang.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident describes a harsh, grating, loud sound or voice.

clue.text: Support I'll back, beset by endless stress

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the trimmed stress encloses the turned piece
endless means the word stress is stripped of both its end letters
back means the letters of I'll are read in reverse order

parts.note: the letters of I'll without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone promises to stand by a friend who is surrounded by constant pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips both ends of stress, 'back' turns I'll round, and 'beset by' sets the turned letters inside the trimmed word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice framework that props up climbing plants, a kind of support.

clue.text: Way the world won't end: in a catastrophe, finally

indicators.note: in places the shortened planet inside the other two pieces
finally picks out the last letter of catastrophe
won't end means the planet loses its final letter

parts.note: Venus is a world, a planet of the solar system

explanation.surface: How the planet escapes destruction: in a disaster, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the world' is a planet, not Earth; 'won't end' docks its last letter, 'finally' takes the end of catastrophe, and 'in' sets the planet between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad road, and figuratively a route or method, so a way.

clue.text: Lack of enthusiasm for one heading off around track

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the shortened word wraps round the track
heading off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: say means for one, for example
a path is a track

explanation.surface: Indifference shown by someone setting off round a running track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' means 'for example'; 'heading off' drops its first letter, and 'around' wraps what is left round the track.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is indifference, the absence of interest or keenness.

clue.text: All steroids in sport? Incompatible

indicators.note: sport as a noun can mean a mutation or freak variant, signalling a reshuffle of the letters

explanation.surface: Performance drugs in athletics are at odds with fair play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' looks like the setting of the scene but is the anagram signal for ALL STEROIDS; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-assorted describes things badly matched that do not go together, so they are mismatched.

clue.text: Right to run away?

definitions.meaning: right means genuine or lawful, legal and above board
a slang phrase for run away is to ...

explanation.surface: Is it all right to flee?
explanation.definitionFit: Legit is slang for legitimate, so right; split as two words it is slang for fleeing on foot.

clue.text: Army doctor has done with cut

indicators.note: cut means the word for done with loses its last letter

parts.note: over means finished, done with

explanation.surface: A military medic has finished with surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army doctor' reads as one unit, but 'Army' is the definition and 'doctor' gives DR.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a large moving crowd or herd, so a multitude, like an army of people.

clue.text: Dance, taking lead in balletic work

indicators.note: the lead in a word is its first letter, here from balletic

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A dancer takes the principal role in a ballet production.
explanation.definitionFit: To bop is to dance energetically to pop music, and a bop is a dance.

clue.text: Good performance at golf a delight, moving last to first

indicators.note: moving last to first means the final letter is shifted to the front

parts.note: glee is great delight

explanation.surface: A golfer's fine round brings joy as they climb from bottom to top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving last to first' takes the E at the end of AGLEE to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, completing a hole in two strokes under par is a fine score with this bird's name.

clue.text: Old fogey to rage about source of expensive body spray

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fogey wraps round the letter

parts.note: a dodo is an old-fashioned person, after the extinct bird

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter, here from expensive

parts.note: to rant is to rage loudly

explanation.surface: A grumpy old man fumes about the cost of a pricey fragrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' gives E from expensive, and 'about' puts it inside DODO after the first D.
explanation.definitionFit: This product is sprayed under the arms to mask odour, so it is a toiletry spray for the body.

clue.text: Utterly wrong about article offering protection

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap round the article
wrong signals that the letters of utterly are put in the wrong order

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news item is entirely mistaken about a guarantee of safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns UTTERLY into TUTELRY, and 'about' wraps that round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelary means acting as a guardian, like a tutelary deity watching over a place.

clue.text: This obliges fellow in good shape to spurn hospitals

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

indicators.note: to spurn is to reject, so the word drops the letters for hospitals

parts.note: to be in good shape is to be healthy
H is the map abbreviation for hospital, twice for hospitals

explanation.surface: A fit man shuns hospitals out of a sense of duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to spurn' takes both H's out of HEALTHY, leaving EALTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Fealty is the loyalty a vassal owed a lord, a duty that binds or obliges him.
